stem: Applying IDLI to mouse embryonic stem cell chromatin, what share of nucleosomes carried DNA accessible within the nucleosome itself?
choices: About 15%
More than 85%
About 40%
Just over 60%
answer: More than 85%
label: Abstract · prevalence of distortion

stem: Why do the authors argue that digestion-based mapping confounds the study of subnucleosomes?
choices: Digestion destroys the histone modifications that mark subnucleosomes
Nuclease cut sites are too sparse to position a fragment near the dyad
One fragment size can arise from a true subnucleosome or from a distorted nucleosome
Digestion releases subnucleosomes faster than it releases intact nucleosomes
answer: One fragment size can arise from a true subnucleosome or from a distorted nucleosome
label: Rationale · why not digestion

stem: What two limits did the authors give for short-read single-molecule methyltransferase footprinting methods such as dSMF?
choices: A 600 bp read-length cap and an inability to methylate linker DNA
A 150 bp read-length cap and MTases specific to GpC or CpG
A 1 kb read-length cap and MTases that methylate only adenines
A 600 bp read-length cap and MTases specific to GpC or CpG
answer: A 600 bp read-length cap and MTases specific to GpC or CpG
label: Rationale · short-read limits

stem: Which enzyme and sequencing platform does the SAMOSA assay combine to footprint chromatin fibres?
choices: The nonspecific adenine MTase EcoGII, read on PacBio
The CpG-specific MTase M.SssI, read on PacBio
The nonspecific adenine MTase EcoGII, read on Oxford Nanopore
The GpC-specific MTase M.CviPI, read on Illumina
answer: The nonspecific adenine MTase EcoGII, read on PacBio
label: Method · SAMOSA components

stem: In the IDLI model, what happens to called footprint sizes as the transition probability t is increased?
choices: They become successively larger, merging adjacent footprints
They become successively smaller, resolving subfootprints
They converge on a single mononucleosome-sized peak
They stay the same size but shift toward the dyad
answer: They become successively smaller, resolving subfootprints
label: Method · the t parameter

stem: What does the acronym IDLI stand for in this work?
choices: Iteratively Detected Loci of Inaccessibility
Inferred Distributions of Linker Inaccessibility
Iteratively Defined Lengths of Inaccessibility
Iteratively Defined Limits of Internal Accessibility
answer: Iteratively Defined Lengths of Inaccessibility
label: Method · what IDLI means

stem: How many sampled nucleosomes and chromatin fibres went into the genome-wide IDLI classification in E14 mouse ES cells?
choices: 571,332 nucleosomes from 145,065 fibres
295,574 nucleosomes from 34,944 fibres
795,765 nucleosomes from 34,944 fibres
795,765 nucleosomes from 145,065 fibres
answer: 795,765 nucleosomes from 145,065 fibres
label: Results · classification input

stem: How many distinct nucleosome types did Leiden clustering of IDLI footprints yield in E14 mouse ES cells?
label: Results · number of types

stem: Which groups of nucleosome types carried some intranucleosomal DNA accessibility, and what fraction of footprints did they hold?
choices: Groups V–VII, holding 86.6% of footprints
Groups II–VII, holding 86.6% of footprints
Groups II–VII, holding 56.3% of footprints
Groups IV–VII, holding 71.2% of footprints
answer: Groups II–VII, holding 86.6% of footprints
label: Results · pervasive distortion

stem: At which superhelical location is the DNA of cluster III-2 nucleosome core particles focally accessible?
choices: SHL ±3.5
SHL ±5
SHL ±2
SHL 0, at the dyad
answer: SHL ±2
label: Results · cluster III-2 geometry

stem: At which superhelical location is the DNA of cluster II-2 nucleosome core particles focally accessible?
choices: SHL ±2
SHL ±6
SHL ±0.5
SHL ±3.5
answer: SHL ±3.5
label: Results · cluster II-2 geometry

stem: What did enrichment in MNase-ChIP hexasome and hemisome fractions establish about the most accessible IDLI groups, V to VII?
choices: They are genuine subnucleosomal species
They are nucleosomes bound by linker histone H1
They are artefacts of EcoGII sequence bias
They are overlapping dinucleosome complexes
answer: They are genuine subnucleosomal species
label: Validation · MNase-ChIP

stem: What does the H1 triple-knockout mouse ES cell model change, and by roughly how much?
choices: Three of six linker histone genes are ablated, removing all linker histone from chromatin
Three of six linker histone genes are ablated, halving linker histone on chromatin
All six linker histone genes are ablated, halving linker histone on chromatin
One of six linker histone genes is ablated, cutting linker histone by a quarter
answer: Three of six linker histone genes are ablated, halving linker histone on chromatin
label: Validation · H1 TKO model

stem: Depletion of group I nucleosomes in H1 triple-knockout cells identified them as what species?
choices: Hexasomes lacking one H2A–H2B dimer
Tetrasomes retaining only the H3–H4 tetramer
Chromatosomes containing linker histone H1
Nucleosomes unwrapped at entry and exit sites
answer: Chromatosomes containing linker histone H1
label: Validation · group I identity

stem: Reconstitutions on Widom 601 arrays suggested that group I nucleosomes in cells are bound by which proteins?
choices: H1 alone, with no other chromatin protein bound
HMGB1 alone, in place of linker histone H1
The ISWI remodeller SNF2h together with H1
H1 together with HMGB1 or another HMG-box protein
answer: H1 together with HMGB1 or another HMG-box protein
label: Validation · in vitro reconstitution

stem: Which transcription factor motif family was enriched in group I (chromatosome) nucleosome types?
choices: Homeodomain
Forkhead / winged helix
C2H2 zinc finger
E-box binding (bHLH)
answer: Homeodomain
label: Motifs · group I

stem: Which motif family was uniquely enriched in the groups II and III nucleosome types with focal intranucleosomal accessibility?
choices: Homeodomain
Forkhead family
C2H2 zinc finger
MADS box
answer: Forkhead family
label: Motifs · groups II and III

stem: Which motif family was enriched in the symmetrically breathing groups IV and V nucleosome types?
choices: Homeodomain
Forkhead / winged helix
E-box binding
C2H2 zinc finger
answer: E-box binding
label: Motifs · groups IV and V

stem: Which motif class was enriched among the shortest footprints that IDLI called, in groups VI and VII?
choices: Homeodomain
Forkhead / winged helix
Nuclear receptor with C4 zinc fingers
C2H2 zinc finger
answer: C2H2 zinc finger
label: Motifs · groups VI and VII

stem: What happened to short footprints at bound CTCF motifs when CTCF protein was acutely degraded?
choices: They were significantly lost
They were significantly gained
They were unchanged while chromatosomes were lost
They shifted away from the motif without changing in number
answer: They were significantly lost
label: CTCF · degron

stem: What did the CTCF motif and degron analyses together suggest about CTCF's effect on nearby nucleosomes?
choices: It favours fully wrapped, inaccessible nucleosome states
It favours partially unwrapped nucleosome states
It evicts nucleosomes without altering those that remain
It recruits linker histone H1 to form chromatosomes
answer: It favours partially unwrapped nucleosome states
label: CTCF · interpretation

stem: What did depleting the cohesin stimulatory factor NIPBL do to nucleosome-type distributions?
choices: Altered them specifically at CTCF sites, mirroring CTCF depletion
Left them unchanged both globally and at CTCF sites
Altered them globally, with no effect specific to CTCF sites
Altered them only at promoters marked by H3K4me3
answer: Altered them globally, with no effect specific to CTCF sites
label: CTCF · cohesin control

stem: Acute SOX2 degradation reduced the proportion of inaccessible nucleosome species — what did the authors infer from this?
choices: SOX2 evicts nucleosomes from its binding sites
SOX2 recruits remodellers that unwrap nearby nucleosomes
SOX2 binding is restricted to nucleosome-free DNA
SOX2 stabilizes nucleosomes in its vicinity
answer: SOX2 stabilizes nucleosomes in its vicinity
label: SOX2 · stabilization

stem: Which nucleosome clusters were significantly enriched in mouse minor satellite sequences?
choices: Clusters I-2 and II-4
Clusters VI and VII
Clusters IV and V-1
Clusters III-1 and III-2
answer: Clusters I-2 and II-4
label: Epigenome · minor satellites

stem: Binning the mouse ES cell transcriptome into expression quintiles, how did nucleosome-type enrichment at transcription start sites behave?
choices: It was flat across quintiles, varying only by domain
It scaled with expression level across the quintiles
It peaked in the middle quintiles and fell at both extremes
It tracked promoter CpG content rather than expression
answer: It scaled with expression level across the quintiles
label: Epigenome · promoter strength

stem: Comparing day 6 endoderm with day 0 iPS cells at bound FOXA2 motifs, which nucleosome types gained representation?
choices: Chromatosomes and fully inaccessible nucleosomes
Short zinc-finger-sized protections alone
Focally accessible core particles and breathable subnucleosomes
Symmetrically unwrapped nucleosomes alone
answer: Focally accessible core particles and breathable subnucleosomes
label: Development · endoderm

stem: Which genetic model did the authors use in primary mouse hepatocytes to test whether FOXA2 shapes nucleosome structure?
choices: A Foxa2 allele lacking its DNA-binding domain, in heterozygotes
A conditional Foxa2 knockout deleting the whole gene in hepatocytes
A degron-tagged FOXA2 allele depleted by dTAG treatment
A Foxa2 allele lacking its nucleosome-interacting domain, in heterozygotes
answer: A Foxa2 allele lacking its nucleosome-interacting domain, in heterozygotes
label: In vivo · FOXA2 model

stem: What did the hepatocyte experiments conclude about the histone-binding domain of FOXA2?
choices: It directly contributes to distortion at FOXA2-bound sites in vivo
It is needed for FOXA2 to reach its motifs but not for distortion
It affects distortion only in differentiating cells, not in mature tissue
It stabilizes chromatosomes without changing core particle accessibility
answer: It directly contributes to distortion at FOXA2-bound sites in vivo
label: In vivo · FOXA2 conclusion

stem: In the single-molecule co-occurrence analysis of trinucleosome stretches, where were homotypic arrangements enriched?
choices: In repressed rather than active epigenomic domains
In active rather than repressed epigenomic domains
In constitutive heterochromatin repeats only
Evenly across domains, with no positional preference
answer: In active rather than repressed epigenomic domains
label: Co-occurrence · homotypic runs

stem: What do the authors say most of the short DNA protections that IDLI classifies are likely to be?
choices: Transcription factors, with a smaller contribution from dimers
H3–H4 tetramers left after dimer loss
H2A–H2B dimers, with a smaller contribution from TFs
Linker histone H1 bound between nucleosomes
answer: H2A–H2B dimers, with a smaller contribution from TFs
label: Limitation · what short footprints are

stem: What do the authors say a comprehensive transcription-factor-specific co-accessibility analysis would require?
choices: Longer sequencing reads spanning whole chromatin domains
A methyltransferase with higher adenine specificity
Degron lines for every factor under study
Greater SAMOSA coverage at the target binding sites
answer: Greater SAMOSA coverage at the target binding sites
label: Limitation · coverage needed

stem: What did detecting an effect in FOXA2 domain-mutant heterozygotes demonstrate about IDLI's sensitivity?
choices: It resolves altered pioneer TF–nucleosome interaction with one functional copy present
It resolves such changes only when the factor is fully absent
It resolves changes in bulk accessibility but not in nucleosome structure
It resolves nucleosome structure only on synthetic template DNA
answer: It resolves altered pioneer TF–nucleosome interaction with one functional copy present
label: Discussion · sensitivity
